overall: At 10:50 ET, Washington DC is sitting at 80.6°F — the running max — with warming essentially stalled (velocity flat at +0.0°F/hr) despite a 2-hour trend of +1.8°F/hr suggesting continued heating is underway. The day is tracking meaningfully below what NWS (93°F) and HRRR (92.8°F) projected, with afternoon convective risk (60% PoP, storms possible 2–3pm) posing a credible cap on further temperature gains.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are sharply split: HRRR and NWS are highly aggressive (92–93°F) while ECMWF (89.9°F) and NBM (87.8°F) are more conservative; the current observed trajectory at ~11am is running cold relative to all of them. The META fusion model — which incorporates intraday observations and is flagged as most reliable — strongly favors 86–87°F (41.9%) and 88–89°F (31.0%), diverging significantly from the D1_NOW top bucket of 90–91°F.
max_temp_prediction: The META model's central tendency points to a high near 87–88°F, consistent with the current +1.8°F/hr 2-hour warming rate applied over the ~4 remaining hours to the predicted 14.5–15.3h peak — which yields roughly 87–88°F before afternoon storm risk arrives. The active Kalshi even-bucket market's top bucket at 90–91°F (62.4% from D1_NOW) appears overpriced relative to META's 10.9% assignment there; the 86–87°F and 88–89°F even buckets look undervalued. Confidence in the 86–89°F range is moderate-to-good given storm timing uncertainty.
